memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is what you are to offer on the altar regularly each day: two lambs a year old. Offer one in the morning and the other at twilight. With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of the finest flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from pressed olives, and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering." - Exodus 29:38-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A lamb every morning and a lamb every evening, day after day, without interruption. The daily offering bracketed Israel's life. However ordinary the day, however busy or uneventful, the day opened and closed with a sacrifice before God.

There is real wisdom in bookending a day this way. Morning and evening, the people were reminded that they lived by atonement and in God's presence. Their whole day sat between two offerings. Nothing they did happened outside that frame.

Our lives have the same shape, though the sacrifice has already been made. Daniel prayed three times a day (Dan 6:10), and the psalmist spoke of evening, morning, and noon crying out to God (Ps 55:17). A rhythm of turning to God at the start and end of each day keeps the whole day framed by Him. If you have no such rhythm, begin simply. A few honest minutes each morning and evening will do more for your soul over a year than occasional intensity. Let your days be bracketed by God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Does my day begin and end with any deliberate turning to God?
What simple rhythm could I start this week and actually sustain?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let my days be framed by You — opened in Your presence and closed in Your care. Give me a steady rhythm of turning to You morning and evening. Amen.
